rationale: Evidence from iteration 10 (score 311.2, best so far): oval now finishes 17 of 20 with progress 0.94, and s-bend (0.11) and slalom (0.07) still stall at the off-track limit, with max_error about 0.06 m on every track. Across the history, each damping increase (kd 0.6 to 0.9) raised progress and cut oscillation on oval (0.31 to 0.20 after the geometry changes). Raising kp alone (iteration 9) did little for the bends, and the speed cut (1.1 to 1.0) helped oval and s-bend. The bends are therefore still overshoot-limited, and the most consistent lever so far is damping. Change: kd 0.9 to 1.2, the only controller change. Speed (1.0), kp (5.0), ki (0.3), sensor layout and wheel track stay fixed so the damping effect can be read cleanly. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error drops below 0.06 on some bends, slalom progress rises above 0.1, and oval completions hold at 15 or more of 20 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.25. Risk: higher kd amplifies sensor noise on the sharpest bends. Hypotheses for the measurements: (H1) if oval oscillation rises above 0.3 and completions fall, kd has passed its useful range and 0.9 is the ceiling. (H2) If s-bend and slalom still stall near 0.1 with max_error at 0.06, the limit is speed on tight bends, not damping, and base_speed should drop to about 0.9 in the next design. (H3) If all tracks survive but none finish, base_speed should rise slightly. This is the final iteration, so the design is chosen to be a safe, evidence-backed step from the best result rather than a large untested change.
